name: BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS) — county unemployment rate
measures: County-level unemployment rate and labor force, from BLS's LAUS program. Series IDs follow the documented LAUCN<state FIPS><county FIPS><measure code> pattern (e.g. LAUCN480150000000003 style construction; exact measure-code suffix for 'unemployment rate' should be re-confirmed against BLS's current docs before coding).
history_available: long monthly history via the flat files at download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/la/ (exact API-accessible depth not confirmed this pass)
cost: free. BLS's own FAQ requires registration for API v2 to get higher limits; a third-party source claims a keyless tier capped at 25 requests/day vs 500/day registered, but this was not confirmed against bls.gov directly. The bulk flat files are also reported (unconfirmed this pass) to 403 requests that don't send an identifying User-Agent header — not literally frictionless even though no key is required; any such User-Agent must not embed any user-identifying information.
license: US government public data, no login wall for the bulk flat files; normal BLS reuse terms (public domain, attribution appreciated but not contractually required for government statistical data).
auth: none for bulk flat-file download; free registration recommended for the JSON API (data.bls.gov/registrationEngine/) to get usable rate limits
recommendation: County unemployment/employment growth is a plausible leading indicator for housing demand and is currently absent from the growth pillar (population_change_10y, income_cagr_10y, bachelors_share_change_10y, age_25_34_share from Census ACS cover demographic trajectory but nothing on jobs). But be honest about granularity: in NYC, 'county' means borough, so this is 5 values spread across roughly 200 NTAs — weak as an intra-NYC differentiator, since neighborhood.py's scoring compares NTAs against each other and a near-flat metric across ~40 NTAs per borough adds little signal. The real value is for the project's stated national-generalization goal, where most other US counties aren't subdivided into dozens of neighborhoods the way NYC boroughs are, so county-level LAUS is a much more meaningful per-area signal elsewhere. Recommend with that caveat made explicit, implemented against the documented bulk flat files (download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/la/la.data.64.County) rather than the rate-limited JSON API.
open_questions: Confirm the correct measure-code suffix for 'unemployment rate' (vs. labor force, employment level, unemployment level) in the LAUCN series ID.

The bulk flat files are reported (unconfirmed) to reject requests without an identifying User-Agent header (403) — confirm, and if real, set one that does not include any user-identifying information.

Decide whether to even bother surfacing this inside NYC itself (5 boroughs, weak signal) vs. only enabling it once the screener covers other metros where county-level actually differentiates neighborhoods.
